highlights.title: The cat-and-mouse game over 3D-printed guns has begun
highlights.summary: The creator of the world's first 3D-printed gun claims he's developed a way to thwart government-mandated software meant to block 3D printers from making firearms. It's an opening volley in what's shaping up to be an evolving battle between regulators trying to stem the tide of ghost guns and…
body: Cody Wilson, who claims to have made the detection-defying tool, is calling it “Hochulization” as a direct jab at New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who pushed through the nation’s first law mandating gun file detection software on new printers earlier this year. “New York is trying to reach into the internet and police how open-source 3D printing is done,” Wilson, who’s based out of Austin, Texas, told The Verge. “I think of it as a self-defense measure.”

The tool is designed to break a relatively simple approach to a 3D-printed gun ban. Wilson’s company, Defense Distributed, runs DEFCAD, the world’s largest 3D gun file repository, which he says hosts over 200,000 files of gun designs and components, such as suppressors. Each of those files can be identified by a hash, a unique string of numbers that’s created by running the file through an algorithm. In theory, a gun file detection system that uses a hashing-based identification method would look for those exact hashes to determine whether a file is a potential gun, flag it, and prevent it from printing.

highlights.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
highlights.summary: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
Can a city’s seawall stand up to a blockbuster storm? Will a region’s power grid hold against record-breaking heat? And can a town’s fire-fighting resources contain a major wildfire?

To answer these questions, communities will first need to know how such extreme events could unfold. How far is a wildfire likely to spread? How much of a region might a storm impact? How long could a heat wave last?

But extreme events are notoriously difficult to anticipate. By their nature, they are outliers. In the history of record keeping, extreme events are sporadic and rare. Yet most methods that assess a region’s risk depend on extreme events of the past to characterize even more extreme, worst-case scenarios in the future.
points: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.

highlights.title: 'We haven't got the money' - Wolff says Mercedes can't match rivals' upgrade rate
highlights.summary: Toto Wolff says Mercedes do not have extra money available to quickly respond to the growing threat from McLaren and Ferrari through car development.
body: The Silver Arrows continue to lead both world championship races, and grew their leads in both standings across the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend, but have seen their early-season dominance eroded in recent months.
After winning the opening six rounds of F1's new rules era, Mercedes have won two races in the last six, the same number as Ferrari and McLaren.

McLaren have taken the last two wins after upgrades to their car at each of the last two events, while Mercedes have brought only smaller revisions to their W17 since its last big update at the Canadian GP in late May.

All teams operate to a yearly budget cap governing car spend, which for 2026 was raised to $215m due to the huge change in regulations, and have to decide how they each allocate spend on car development through the season.

highlights.title: Tom Hardy’s $478M Sci-Fi Action Movie Officially Surges to #2 on Netflix
highlights.summary: Over the years, Tom Hardy has proven to be one of the most versatile actors around. He's starred in Oscar-winning dramas like Alejandro Iñárritu's The Revenant and led blockbuster smash hits like Mad Max: Fury Road.
body: Fresh off the success of Spider-Man: Homecoming, Sony launched its own Spider-Man Universe in 2018 with Venom. Tom Hardy was cast in the dual lead roles of Eddie Brock and Venom (previously portrayed by Topher Grace in Sam Rami’s Spider-Man 3 ). The prospect of a movie about a Spider-Man villain that didn't include Spider-Man was a weird pitch, and Hardy delivered an equally unconventional performance to match. It's that charming commitment to the role that made Venom a cult hit.

Fans especially latched onto the romantic side of Eddie and Venom's relationship, which 2021's Venom: Let There Be Carnage would lean into. While Sony's other Spider-Man Universe films like Morbius and Madame Web crashed and burned, becoming fodder for endless memes, Venom persisted. In 2024, Hardy returned for Venom: The Last Dance, which is now the second-most streamed movie on Netflix.

body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: Problems brewing for the proper pint as Camra membership falls
highlights.summary: Cost of living has hit campaign group while multinationals are threatening to squeeze out independent breweries. For centuries, the wooden real ale pump has been the hallmark of a good British boozer.
body: Real ale is a traditional draught cask beer, a “living” product that is produced and stored in its cask. It differs from a cold, fizzy lager, in which the yeast is killed and carbon dioxide is added. Real ale contains live yeast so it continues fermenting until it is served.

Outside the Devonshire pub in Soho, central London, there is an ever-present horde of drinkers downing pints of Guinness, a stout made by the multinational company Diageo. But the landlord and co-owner Oisín Rogers says: “Real ale is all I drink.”

He says: “It is a properly handmade British product produced in exactly the same way it has been for centuries. It has never been industrialised like some of the other drinks that are for sale in bars in London.” His favourite tipple, is, appropriately, a pint of Landlord, made by the family-owned Timothy Taylor brewery in Keighley, West Yorkshire.

Tom Stainer, Camra’s chief executive, says independent breweries are facing unfair competition from multinationals. If you walk into a pub on the high street, you are often confronted with the same few beers, most of which are made by the same large companies, Stainer says.

highlights.summary: The federal government is expanding a safety investigation into a number of vehicles manufactured by General Motors after receiving hundreds of reports of brake failure.
body: GM says that in the event of that happening, the car should still retain a number of critical safety features—antilock brakes, traction control, and stability control—at least until it comes to a complete stop, at which point they become inoperable. But NHTSA’s ODI says that it has received many reports that contradict this behavior and allege that eBoost failures are followed by an immediate loss of braking, which obviously poses a safety risk.

Indeed, NHTSA has received 227 incident reports, a number that grows to 745 once you include the hundreds of occurrences reported to GM. Twenty-two cases resulted in crashes, and while six people have been injured in five crashes, thankfully there have been no fatal incidents.

NHTSA says that the following vehicles are equipped with eBoost: “2023-2026 MY Cadillac Lyriq, Chevrolet Colorado, and GMC Canyon; 2024-2026 MY Buick Enclave, Envision; Chevrolet Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Traverse; Cruise Origin; and GMC Acadia; 2025-2026 MY Cadillac Celestiq and Optiq. ODI is also aware of 2024-2026 MY Acura ZDX and 2024-2026 MY Honda Prologue vehicles that were built with this system.”

highlights.title: How to encourage smarter AI use in the classroom
highlights.summary: This article is from Making AI Work, MIT Technology Review’s limited-run newsletter examining how to apply LLMs across industries. To receive it in your inbox, sign up here. Chatbots took many schools by surprise upon their release a few years ago.
body: Nevertheless, the generative AI boom increased the burden on teachers, who were already working long hours to plan lessons, make homework assignments, and grade exams, and now needed to adapt to a new technology. For many, it still feels like there’s no clear path forward. Organizations ranging from OpenAI to UNESCO encourage AI use in the classroom, but many teachers feel confused about how exactly to handle it.

Cheshire Academy is a private boarding and day school in Connecticut with about 400 students in grades 9 through 12. Administrators there don’t force instructors to use AI at all, though the school’s librarian and technology coordinator George Aiello claims the “vast majority” of instructors use it in some way. The educators there are trying a patchwork of programs, including general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT and Perplexity as well as more specialized tools like MagicSchool, an AI-powered platform meant specifically for educators.

highlights.title: 38 Years Later, The Best 'Calvin and Hobbes' Mom Quote Is Still Unmatched in Comic Strip History
highlights.summary: Calvin’s mom doesn't get enough credit. Within Bill Watterson’s classic comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin’s mom, who is a homemaker, is Calvin’s number one nurturer and the person preparing nearly all of his meals (which Calvin definitely doesn’t appreciate).
body: There’s a ton of love for Calvin’s dad. People love that, just for his own amusement, Calvin's dad will make up absurd lies, like when Calvin asks his dad where babies come from, only for his dad to say “Most people just go to Sears, buy the kit, and follow the assembly instructions.” But Calvin’s mom — who, like Calvin’s dad, has no name — doesn’t get nearly as much love. Even Watterson himself has admitted that he underserved the character.

“Calvin's mom is the daily disciplinarian, a job that taxes her sanity, so I don't think we get to see her at her best,” Watterson once explained. “I regret that the strip mostly shows her impatient side, but I try to hint at other aspects of her personality and her interests by what she's doing when Calvin barges in.”

Calvin’s mom can be just as funny as his dad, and it usually comes when the strip shows her impatient side. So to show her a bit of the respect that is so well deserved, we’ve decided to track down her best ever quote from the comic strip, and share a bit more of what’s so great about her along the way.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: 10 Perfectly Written High Fantasy Books for Fans of Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones
highlights.summary: George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire proved that high fantasy doesn’t have to be synonymous with high magic. Most people in the Seven Kingdoms don’t expect to meet a dragon or giant, making it all the more terrifying when those mythical creatures appear.
body: J.R.R. Tolkien effectively established the genre of high fantasy when he came up with the world of Middle-earth and populated it with fantastical creatures facing an apocalyptic threat in The Lord of the Rings. While numerous stories introduce talking animals, fairies, or demons to a version of the real world — or even see regular people stepping into a magical realm they previously didn’t know existed — high fantasy takes place in a fully imaginary reality with its own rules, history, and factions.

One of the true masters of the genre, Ursula K. Le Guin both drew upon and subverted the classic tropes of fantasy stories. Ged, a young boy with great magical potential, has to grapple with his own impatience and hubris rather than a dark lord. The story of a boy sent to wizarding school set the stage for Harry Potter, but A Wizard of Earthsea is a far more thoughtful tale as Ged is constantly tempted by great power but must learn to avoid easy shortcuts in order to maintain balance in himself and the world. It’s an extremely quick read, so pick up the rest of the five-book series for more beautiful and meditative stories.

French President Emmanuel Macron hailed the move as on a scale not seen "since Disneyland Paris", and added "you know my interest for manga".
An opening date for the parks - which will be built near Cergy-Pontoise - has not set by the Élysée Palace, but they will open in stages and construction is expected to take years.

highlights.summary: Chinese retailer AliExpress has been caught fingerprinting visitors after one of the metrics—an outdated technique that measures inaudible sounds it sends to browsers—impeded a researcher's ability to use his bluetooth headphones.
body: Researcher Matthew Callaghan said he stumbled on the stealthy tracking by mistake. After loading the AliExpress homepage, audio from his phone stopped playing over his multipoint headphones, which accept connections from more than one device at a time. He set the headphones to play sounds from his phone except when his PC was producing audio. Each time he loaded AliExpress, the phone audio stopped. Each time he closed the tab the site was loaded into, the phone was once again audible.

While investigating the odd behavior, Callaghan said he found two highly obfuscated scripts. Together, they rendered a graph that analyzed the WebAudio readings of each visiting browser. This graph acted as an oscillator that measured Sawtooth waves, which are common in output from digital audio.

“The oscillator generates a known waveform,” Callaghan wrote. “The analyser measures the result after it has passed through the browser’s audio implementation, and the script reads frequency data from it.”

highlights.title: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns
highlights.summary: Early testers are raving about what Instinct can do, but some say the AI assistant’s sweeping access, broad terms and ability to act on users’ behalf come with uncomfortable trade-offs
body: To be fair, Instinct is still in private testing for now, so these concerns haven’t yet scaled to the wider public at this time.

Created by a small team led by former Sierra research scientist Noah Shinn, San Francisco-based Instinct is operated by Spear Street Technology, per its terms and California business filings. It’s currently operating in stealth, per PitchBook.

The AI agent itself works by connecting to your applications and devices, including your email, messaging apps, calendar, and your device’s audio, location, screen, and more. You can text the agent or call it via text message or WhatsApp, asking it to perform various tasks for you, like booking your appointments and reservations, scheduling a ride to the airport, cleaning up your inbox, organizing important information, handling your shopping, finding you cheap flights, and much more.

Though Instinct is described by testers as outperforming their expectations, some have also raised concerns about the company’s approach to customer privacy and security. This raises a timely question: are the trade-offs of giving AI this level of access and autonomy actually worth it?

body: The 22-year-old Elias – known as Allan – made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. He is yet to play for Brazil.

highlights.title: Is Sleeping Under Canvas the Secret to Better Rest?
highlights.summary: Here’s why traveling to sleep in a tent could improve your sleep patterns long after you check out—plus, five of the best places in the world to do it.
body: For something so fundamental, sleep has become surprisingly complicated. We track it, optimize it, travel in search of it—fueling a fast-growing sleep tourism industry built on blackout blinds, circadian lighting, and AI-calibrated mattresses. And yet, for all this innovation, the most effective reset often lies in something far simpler: stepping outside, and more specifically, sleeping under canvas.

I’ve felt it myself, in ways no hotel room, however luxurious, has ever quite managed to replicate. From bedding down to the lullabies of the bush in fly camps across wild corners of Africa, to a WiFi-free ranch in Wyoming with a what-dreams-are-made-of glamping meadow: the steady rush of a snow-melt creek just beyond my tent, a constant thread of white noise that softened everything around it. After days spent entirely outdoors, moving my body, with almost zero screen time—whether on safari or in the saddle, moving through vast landscapes, syncing to the sunset and the stars—the effect was the same. I slept more deeply, woke more easily, and felt, for once, properly rested.

highlights.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with weekend of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
highlights.summary: Possession numbers, the intense physicality and the pure rhythm of games all felt noticeably new as the season began. There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip-drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go.
body: So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

highlights.summary: It sounds like fans were eager to learn everything they could about From Software's The Duskbloods, as one of the game's producers has revealed the Switch 2 exclusive saw higher playtest sign-ups compared to Elden Ring Nightreign.
body: Speaking during a livestream hosted by Japanese gaming publication Famitsu (and translated by GamesRadar+ ), From Software producer Yasuhiro Kitao stated the number of applications for The Duskbloods playtest eclipsed that of the developer's previous multiplayer experiment.

Given that Elden Ring Nightreign's playtest was available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S (the full game was also available on PC and last-gen consoles) the fact that The Duskbloods received more interest on Switch 2 sounds like it should be impossible. The Switch 2 is also a relatively new console, having only been available for around a year, meaning its user base is much smaller compared to that of the other two consoles.

While it is surprising on the surface, perhaps there is some logic to be deciphered here. Elden Ring Nightreign went on to sell more than 5 million copies, with its DLC alone selling 2 million copies in under a week. The game's popularity and success proved From Software could make a wildly fun, multiplayer-focused souls-like, perhaps generating more interest for The Duskbloods.

highlights.title: ‘Survivor’ vs. ‘The Traitors’: Will Emmy Voters Finally Give the Original Reality Juggernaut Its Due?
highlights.summary: “The Traitors” has won more Emmys in three years than “Survivor” has won in 25. It’s not close, either. Since arriving on Peacock, Alan Cumming’s Scottish castle whodunit has banked eight total Emmys — a casting win before it ever cracked the marquee race, back-to-back reality competition trophies…
body: When “Survivor” premiered in the summer of 2000, it drew 51 million viewers to its season finale, which crowned Richard Hatch the first-ever Sole Survivor. The Academy created the reality competition program Emmy in 2003, in direct response to the boom “Survivor” ignited. Then it handed the inaugural trophy to its CBS sister series “The Amazing Race.” “Survivor” lost to “The Amazing Race” four straight times from 2003 to 2006, before it did something stranger than losing: It completely disappeared.

For 16 consecutive years, the biggest brand in the genre couldn’t even get nominated — from 2007 through 2022. That stretch included the “Cook Islands” and first Fiji seasons (Seasons 13 and 14), which crowned Yul Kwon — in the first season to feature a final three instead of a final two, a format that coincidentally included Season 50 contestant Ozzy Lusth — and Earl Cole, who became the first unanimous winner in the show’s history.

highlights.title: Chang-rae Lee's Guide to Umbria
highlights.summary: In late 2019, the author—whose new novel is out this month—and his wife purchased a modest former farm property in northern Umbria. Here, he reveals highlights of the region.
body: While he has yet to write about the region, he finished his two novels in the old stone house “that’s always cool even in the high summer heat,” including this month’s A Tender Age (Riverhead), about a child of Korean immigrants navigating adolescence.

“Although we don’t venture out every day, over the years we’ve explored much of this area of the Upper Tiber River Valley, the Alto Tevere,” he says. Here, wisdom he’s gained as a result of that exploration.

Restaurants: Our houseguests always ask this first, because of course eating well is a primary objective when here. Because black summer truffles are usually abundant in Umbria, I steer folks to two truffle-centric eateries, Da Baffone, which is perched far up in the hills above the medieval town of Gubbio, and the more easily accessed Osteria del Boccajolo in Umbertide. Both places will shock you with the abundance of truffle shavings that practically covers the handmade tagliatelle, or the scrambled eggs, and even the steak. Amazing stuff.

body: Existing investors including Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst are also participating in the round. The fresh funds would come just weeks after General Intuition raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation.
The news confirms earlier reporting on the deal for what is becoming one of the hottest startups tackling physical AI.

CEO Pim de Witte spun out General Intuition last October from his video game clip-sharing platform Medal, using its hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay and “action labels” — records of which buttons a player pressed and when — as an initial dataset.

Investor Vinod Khosla recently told TechCrunch that he believes those action labels will be a key part of the “emergence of intuition,” or the ability for a model to truly generalize across tasks that it wasn’t explicitly trained on.

highlights.title: Amazon and Twitch Face Class Action Lawsuit After Introducing Opt-Out Setting That Uses Streamers' Content to Train AI
highlights.summary: Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they manually opt out. The setting sparked a wave of backlash when it was rolled out last week.
body: It’s buried in users’ security and privacy settings, and is automatically turned on by default. Streamers must toggle the option off in order to opt out of it — but that doesn’t stop Twitch from using their channel content for other purposes, as outlined in the platform’s Privacy Notice.

“Defendants’ actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation," the suit reads.

"Content creators such as Plaintiff and the Class Members will never be able to claw back the intellectual property unlawfully copied and used by Defendants to train Amazon’s generative AI. Once AI ingests content, that content is stored in its neural network, and not capable of deletion or retraction. Defendants’ actions constitute abuse and exploitation of content creators’ work for Defendants’ profit."

Damages sought include “all available contract damages, including actual, compensatory, consequential, and nominal damages, together with such other relief as the Court deems just and proper,” though no specific monetary amount was mentioned.

highlights.title: Vogue’s Guide to Monte Carlo, From the Casino to the Côte d’Azur
highlights.summary: For more than a century, Monte Carlo has drawn artists, aristocrats, gamblers, and the international beau monde. Here’s how to experience it now.
body: “Europe has one Eldorado—Monte Carlo! It is nothing but a rock, yet it is a realm where Illusion is queen. The skies and sea, there, are blue more often than elsewhere, and time suspends its flight, for roulette turns much faster than the hands of a watch.” So began a dispatch from Monte Carlo in the May 1936 issue of Vogue.

By then, the magazine had already been chronicling life on this tiny patch of the Mediterranean for decades. In 1917, with Europe at war, Vogue reported—under the wonderfully improbable headline “Monte Carlo Is as Gay as—Monte Carlo”—on a social season that carried on nonetheless. That same year, Puccini’s La rondine had its world premiere at the Opéra de Monte-Carlo, one chapter in a performing-arts history that Vogue would follow through decades of opera and ballet.

It is nothing but a rock, yet it is a realm where Illusion is queen.
So began a dispatch from Monte Carlo in the May 1936 issue of Vogue.
In 1917, with Europe at war, Vogue reported—under the wonderfully improbable headline “Monte Carlo Is as Gay as—Monte Carlo”—on a social season that carried on nonetheless.
